title: Jubilee 2000
hookLine: churches campaigned to cancel poor countries' debts, citing Leviticus 25

lines: AN OLD LAW, A MODERN CAMPAIGN.
cards: Fifty years, then a trumpet. In the book of Leviticus, Israel is told to count seven times seven years, and then, on the day of atonement, to sound the trumpet through the whole land. What follows is a startling law.
A field sold in a bad year goes back to the family that lost it. People who had sold themselves into service go home.
Much later, churches and aid groups picked up that trumpet and pointed it at something modern: the debts weighing on poor countries. They named their campaign after the old law.

teach.h: PROCLAIM LIBERTY THROUGHOUT ALL THE LAND.
teach.b: The law is in Leviticus 25. The fiftieth year is holy, and the King James Bible gives the command: "proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you."

teach.h: THE LAND IS MINE: YOU ARE GUESTS.
teach.b: The reason comes a few verses on, spoken by God: "for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me." Nobody owns the ground forever. Everyone is a guest on it.
Wealth can pile up for a while, but not for good. Deuteronomy has a smaller cousin of the idea: "At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release," a letting go of debts between neighbors.
The honest part: some readers note that the rest of the Bible tells no story of a jubilee being kept. The idea traveled anyway.
In Luke, Jesus reads from Isaiah in his hometown and announces "the acceptable year of the Lord," and some readers hear a jubilee in it.
Christians who pray the Lord's Prayer in Matthew's words say: "forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors."
Christian groups, joined by people of other faiths and none, argued that old loans were pressing on countries that could barely pay for their own clinics and schools, and that a fresh start was owed.
They gathered signatures, held vigils and marched. Some debts were later written off; others were not, and people still argue about what helped.

teach.h: AN OLD LAW IN THE FINANCE MINISTRY.
teach.b: But a line from an ancient law about farmland had walked into the rooms where finance ministers meet.

how: Churches and Christian aid groups campaign and pray for debt relief for poor countries, often drawing on the jubilee of Leviticus 25 and the line "forgive us our debts" from the Lord's Prayer.

o: a yearly feast of thanks for the harvest
a holy fiftieth year when debts were let go
a royal party marking a king's long reign

games.q: the old law and the new campaign — tap the pairs.
p: a jubile: the field goes home
a campaign to cancel poor countries' debts

s: in Leviticus, the jubilee comes every seventh year
after seven times seven years, the fiftieth year is hallowed as the jubile. the seven-year release of debts is Deuteronomy's smaller cousin.
the jubilee was only about forgiving money
land went back to the family that lost it, and people who had sold themselves into service went home.
the Lord's Prayer in Matthew asks forgiveness for debts
"forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors."

games.q: you sold your family's field in a bad year. now the fiftieth year has come, and the trumpet sounds through the land. what happens to the field?
o: the buyer keeps it forever; a sale is a sale.
it goes back to your family.
you may buy it back at double the price.
games.why: Leviticus 25: in the jubilee, every man returns to his possession. the reason given is surprising: the land was never anyone's to sell forever. "the land is mine."

practice: Bring to mind a debt, not only money, that has sat on the table a long time, and hold it without adding it up; then widen the circle to a country carrying something it cannot lift.
If you pray, you can pray the line from Matthew, forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors; if you don't, just let the word release sit with you.

wordCard.voice: Jubilee. The fiftieth year in Leviticus, when debts were let go and lost land went home, the ancient law that named a modern campaign to cancel poor countries' debts.

orig.note: Hebrew: the word Leviticus 25 uses for the fiftieth year, the jubilee.

carryVoice: Your line: proclaim liberty. The field goes home, and the land stays God's. See you tomorrow.
